Swarm Intelligence for Morphogenetic Engineering · study notes
Source-linked reconstruction (2026-11-26). The original lesson file was not found in the recovered archives. These are newly authored study notes, not the original text.

Bruce J. MacLennan and Allen C. McBride, Swarm Intelligence for Morphogenetic Engineering, 2019, arXiv:1908.08787. https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.08787

Morphogenetic engineering investigates how many agents can coordinate to construct structured systems across spatial scales. MacLennan and McBride use mathematical abstractions of embryonic development rather than requiring artificial agents to reproduce biological detail. Their Morphgen notation describes spatial fields and their changing values using partial differential equations. Their examples cover routing fiber bundles with modified flocking, and producing segmented body structures with interacting timing and spatial processes. They also discuss deriving individual-agent behavior from a global continuum specification using a variation of smoothed particle hydrodynamics. These are research methods, not evidence that this software implements Morphgen or physical microrobots.

Design exercise for the existing Synthia swarm: specify a host objective as an observable check on state. Distinguish active units, passive resources, local observations, permissible operations and constraints. Let units construct a candidate from the actual primitive repertoire. Test a controlled failure, then compare the corrected candidate against multiple initial states. Preserve a verified descendant in the host while retaining the original swarm and its acquired ability. Record the state transition, participating unit identities, formation, evidence, and result. This is the project's computational lifecycle, not a claim of equivalence to the paper's physical model.

For evaluation, compare a local interaction policy with a baseline on the same tasks; record completion, error, collisions, resource cost and generalization to new initial conditions. Keep failed cases in the evidence rather than treating visual similarity as successful execution. For a neighborhood-based recognizer, test whether learned formation labels remain useful as density, orientation and radius change. Separate observation and classification from the control policy that actually performs the task.

Project sources: morphogenesis.js, organism_swarm.js, gameenginex_morph.js, hostworld.js, and the original morphogen-swarm-lab recognizer. Study-note reconstruction and proposed exercises are explicitly distinguished from original donor source and existing verified behavior.
